governanceNotes: D1 batch 66 (2026-09-26): identity deferred (DIRECTION-INVERSION plus SHARED-SUBSTRATE plus no-located-downstream-outcome). Oral hairy leukoplakia is a lesion marker of systemic immunosuppression rather than a disease with its own secondary-condition pathways: (i) HIV association direction - OHL is documented as a sentinel manifestation of advanced HIV infection (PMID 41552200), so the causal arrow runs immunosuppression to lesion; an OHL-to-hiv-aids edge would invert that direction and duplicate the published hiv-aids window's own outgoing scope (the hiv-aids identity carries suggestions to uveitis and peripheral-neuropathy and would be the primary in any OHL relationship; direction-inversion guard); (ii) oral candidiasis coinfection - candidiasis frequently co-occurs in the same immunosuppressed hosts but the located literature treats co-occurrence as shared-substrate immunosuppression marker association, not a direct candidal-to-EBV or EBV-to-candidal pathway (shared-substrate guard; not authored); (iii) malignant transformation - oral hairy leukoplakia is an EBV epithelial proliferation without premalignant standing; zero located quantification of transformation to oral cancer (the published leukoplakia and erythroplakia oral-cancer windows are homonymous white-lesion evidence and do not transfer); (iv) asymptomatic course - OHL is typically discovered on examination without functional sequela, and the located topical-treatment and sentinel-manifestation literature quantifies lesion persistence and diagnostic value rather than downstream morbidity; (v) pharyngeal extension or dysphagia - no located quantification. Reopening conditions: (a) an OHL cohort quantifying a catalog-fit downstream outcome with HIV severity, CD4 count, and antiretroviral status adjusted; or (b) a governance decision placing OHL under the hiv-aids window as a documented manifestation rather than a standalone mapping source.
